# Largest Odd Number in String. An empty result is written "".

@example Every odd piece ends at the 7 or at the 1, and 71 is the largest of them.
"7148260"
=> "71"

@example All four digits are even, so no piece is odd.
"2864"
=> ""

@example The last digit is odd, so the whole string is the answer.
"903"
=> "903"

# A single digit, odd or even.
"9"
=> "9"

"0"
=> ""

# Several odd digits: the answer ends at the rightmost one, not at the
# leftmost one or at the largest one.
"9312"
=> "931"

# Each odd digit as the rightmost odd one, followed by zeros.
"30"
=> "3"

"4450"
=> "445"

"8770"
=> "877"

"62900"
=> "629"

# Odd digits at both ends with even ones between: the whole string.
"7246809"
=> "7246809"

# Zeros inside the answer, and even digits after it.
"5000300486"
=> "50003"

# 10016 digits, more than a buffer sized for 10^4 holds: the last odd
# digit, a 7, is thirteenth from the end, followed by 000 and more even
# digits, so the answer has 10004 digits.
""
=> ""

# 2500 digits, all even.
""
=> ""

# 3000 digits, and only the first one is odd.
""
=> "1"

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"4100533"
=> "4100533"

@gen 2 small
"20084"
=> ""

@gen 3 small
"37306040"
=> "373"

@gen 4 small
"1478"
=> "147"

@gen 5 small
"644698"
=> "64469"

@gen 6 small
"48"
=> ""
